ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $C$ is on the line segment $AB$. Through point $B$, a line $l \perp AB$ is drawn, and point $P$ is a point on line $l$. Connect $AP$, and point $Q$ is the midpoint of $AP$. Draw $QR \perp AB$ with the foot of the perpendicular being $R$. Connect $CQ$, with $AC=2$, $BC=1$, and $CQ=1$. What is the length of $CR$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that, $QR\perp AB$ and $l\perp AB$, \\
$\therefore QR\parallel BP$, \\
$\therefore \frac{AQ}{AP}=\frac{AR}{AB}$, \\
As point Q is the midpoint of AP, \\
$\therefore \frac{AQ}{AP}=\frac{AR}{AB}=\frac{1}{2}$, \\
Also given that $AC=2$ and $BC=1$, \\
$\therefore AB=3$, \\
$\therefore AR=\frac{3}{2}$, \\
$\therefore CR=AC-AR=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB is a horizontal line segment, A is on the left and B is on the right; C is located on AB, and the visible order from left to right is A, R, C, B. Through B there is a vertical straight line l, P is on l; AP is a slanted line, Q is on AP; from Q a perpendicular is drawn to AB, with foot R; CQ is also connected in the figure. Reasoning: Because QR ⟂ AB, and the straight line l on which BP lies is also ⟂ AB, QR ∥ BP. In triangle ABP, Q is the midpoint of AP, and QR ∥ BP, therefore triangle AQR and triangle APB are similar, hence AR/AB = AQ/AP = 1/2. From AC=2 and BC=1, AB=AC+BC=3, so AR=3/2. Also from the figure R is located between A and C, so CR=AC−AR=2−3/2=1/2.
